title: Model onboarding CI: verifiable artifacts and staged profile rollouts
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: Define and implement a CI orchestration pattern for onboarding new model artifacts into the model catalog that ensures artifacts are cryptographically verifiable, reproducible, and released through staged performance-profile rollouts (canary -> ramp -> full). This ticket covers the pipeline orchestration, artifact attestation metadata, runtime pinning semantics, automatic smoke/perf validation, and an operator-friendly promotion workflow.
acceptance_criteria: On PR merge to main: a reproducible model artifact is built, hashed, and published to the model artifact registry with an attached attestation (signature + metadata).
The model catalog entry auto-creates a draft profile with baseline perf metrics computed by the CI perf harness (latency P50/P95, memory, token throughput).
A gated canary rollout can be triggered that routes <=5% of traffic to the new model variant; telemetry shows no degradation beyond defined thresholds within 24 hours.
Operator can progress the rollout to 25%, 50%, then 100% via a single promotion command or console button; rollback is possible and documented.
All artifacts include provenance metadata: source repo commit, build inputs, toolchain versions, and KMS-backed signature fingerprint.
implementation_plan: Prototype pipeline using GitHub Actions to produce a canonical artifact (tar + manifest). Use deterministic build flags and pinned Python/LDK containers to maximize reproducibility.
Attach an attestation to the artifact using Cosign (OCI signing) with keys managed via KMS; store signatures in the artifact registry alongside the image/manifest.
Extend the model catalog API to accept signed artifact manifests and extract provenance fields (commit, model-id, model-version, quantization tags, build hash).

Integrate the CI perf harness to run a short benchmark suite (100 short prompts + one long prompt) and publish a performance profile to a staging bucket; fail the pipeline if regressions >10% against baseline.

Build a rollout controller that coordinates traffic split updates: start at 5% for 24h, evaluate telemetry (error rate, P95 latency, model-quality regression), then allow manual or automated progression to higher percentages.
Expose an operator CLI and Console action to approve promotions; all promotions produce an audit entry with the acting user and ticket reference.
Add e2e tests: simulate model artifact arrival, validate signature verification, ensure catalog shows profile, and run a canary promotion with synthetic traffic.
notes: Design decision: prefer OCI-style signing (Cosign) over custom PKI to leverage community tooling and avoid building verification logic from scratch.
We will not attempt full SLSA attestation v2 in phase 1; instead capture equivalent provenance fields and the signature fingerprint so we can iterate to formal SLSA later.
Trade-off: keeping the perf harness short reduces CI cost but increases risk of missing edge regressions; mitigations include longer nightly runs and post-promotion regression alerts.
Runtime pinning will use model-id + semantic version (e.g., model:gptx:1.2.0) and an immutable artifact hash for strict pins. The catalog will map versions to artifact hashes.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Ava Nguyen: Initial ticket created after architecture sync. Goal: replace ad-hoc onboarding scripts with repeatable CI flow that enforces minimal security controls.
2026-03-03 — Diego Martinez: PoC pipeline committed to feature/ci-prototype. Used deterministic build container; still need KMS integration for signing.

2026-03-05 — Priya Shah (Security): Reviewed signing approach. Security prefers KMS-backed keys and rotation policy. Asked to provide key access matrix and operator workflow for emergency key retirements.
2026-03-08 — Diego Martinez: Switched to Cosign + KMS; prototype now publishes signature alongside OCI artifact. Added catalog webhook to ingest manifests.

2026-03-10 — Mei Chen (SRE): Raised concern about rollout controller interacting with autoscaler. Added a safety gate: rollout controller queries current node capacity and will not increase canary percent if autoscaler reports low headroom.

2026-03-12 — Diego Martinez: Perf harness integrated with CI. Short benchmark runs in ~7m; initial model failed perf gate on P95 latency (regression +18%). Rolled back automatically and left a draft profile in catalog for further tuning. Next actions: investigate runtime kernel selection and quantization flags used in build.
